answer.headline: What RUMIN holds on Aerisca Airways

blocks.text: Aerisca Airways is a fictional company in RUMIN's knowledge graph [E1]. RUMIN's record describes it as “Fictional Indian full-service airline” [E1].

The graph states 4 paths by which 4 economic variables reach it: 4 through costs [E2]. They start from Brent crude oil price, Jet fuel price (U.S. Gulf Coast), U.S. effective federal funds rate and USD/INR exchange rate [E2].

Its latest stored scenario execution, “Oil, rupee and rates on Aerisca” (version 1), simulated profit before tax falling by 6,700,000 INR over 12 months [E11]. That is a simulated result under the scenario's changes and entered figures, not a forecast.
Financial Intelligence lists 20 findings for it [E13]; the first reads “Official exchange rate (INR per US$, period average) — India rose 9.38 %” (evidence grade observed) [E14].

airline_fuel_cost: Fuel is consumed evenly through the year: each month uses one twelfth of the annual volume, and annual revenue and costs accrue evenly.
airline_fuel_cost: The fuel bill is consumption × the benchmark jet fuel price × the exchange rate. Taxes, fees and supplier margins that do not follow the benchmark are outside the model.

airline_fuel_cost: Scenario changes are step changes: they take effect in the start month and last for the stated duration (to the end of the horizon unless one is set), after which the changed variables return to their baselines. Every change in a run shares this timing.

airline_fuel_cost: Jet fuel responds to crude oil with a constant elasticity β after a lag: ln(jet fuel) changes by β × ln(1 + crude change). With β = 1 the refining margin stays a constant proportion of the price.
airline_fuel_cost: Hedged fuel pays the baseline US-dollar price until the hedges expire; the exchange rate is not hedged; hedges are not rolled over.
airline_fuel_cost: Fares recover a fixed share of the change in fuel cost after a lag, for rises and falls alike, and passenger demand does not respond.
airline_fuel_cost: The exchange rate affects the fuel bill only: other dollar costs and any dollar revenue are outside the model.
